Looping you in — forwarding DataSpring’s SOW v3 and Q1 usage. Key asks for internal review:

- Procurement / Finance (Markus): confirm whether the 24-month / 10% platform fee reduction is favorable vs our preferred 12-month cadence. Also check how overage billing aligns with our billing systems (per-10k rows).
- Legal (Laura): please check the SLA wording (delivery success, latency) and any data residency / processing clauses. We need standard Redwood data handling clauses applied plus SOC2 evidence.
- Karthik: want your input on negotiation levers: target discount, credit terms, and whether a committed uplift makes sense given projected usage growth.

Proposed negotiation targets: 20% off list for a 12-month renewal or 10% + $25k credit for 24-month. Push to get a 30-day invoice term, and explicit commitment on schema change notification (60 days).

I scheduled an internal pre-call for Mon 24 May 10:30am PT to align. DataSpring proposed Tue/Wed next week for vendor sync; I’ll confirm once we align.

Thanks,
Monica

Reviewed SOW v3 — top-line legal items:

1) Data processing addendum: add explicit Redwood-approved subprocessors list and SOC2 attestation frequency (annual).
2) Schema & change management: require 60-day notice for breaking changes and a mitigation window of 14 days for production-impacting changes.
3) Liability cap: propose capping at two times fees for breach; remove carve-outs that expose us for downstream consumer losses.
4) SLA credits: make them automatic and measurable (tokens / rows affected) rather than discretionary.

I’ll prepare a redline and ask contracts@dataspring.ai for a clean MS Word with tracked changes. Negotiation priorities: keep the 12-month option as primary, push hard for the 25% discount target Karthik suggested, and insist on a documented data incident playbook from CS.

Laura Bennett
